items.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
items.summary: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.
items.author: Yuanjie Ren, Margarita Davydova, Shankar Balasubramanian et al.

items.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
items.summary: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. Their joint analysis requires their cross-covariance. We derive it within the halo model and show it is a super-sample effect: only the monopole of an individual DM correlates with the angular power spectrum, yielding an exact, model-independent bound on the correlation coefficient. We validate the calculation against log-normal forward simulations of $10^4$ FRBs.
items.author: Amy Wayland, Robert Reischke

items.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
items.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs.
items.author: Aldana Al-Sulaiti, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Muhammad Bilal Akram Dastagir et al.

items.title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
items.summary: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry.
items.author: Ke-Sean J. M. Peter, Ryan A. Kowalski, David A. Curie et al.

items.title: Testing the Spin of New Physics with Top Precision Measurements
items.summary: Precision measurements can reveal not only the presence of new physics, but also information about the dynamics that generated it. We study this question in top-pair production by comparing three top-philic scenarios: a colored scalar top partner, a colored vector-like fermion, and a spin-one $Z^\prime$ mediator. The first two contribute through loop corrections, while the $Z^\prime$ contributes at tree level. We show that the scalar and vector-like fermion scenarios match onto the same effective operator structure at low energies,making their distinction unfeasible using the EFT approach. However, near or above threshold their full loop amplitudes develop distinct momentum-dependent interference patterns.
items.author: André Lessa, Vinícius Rocca, Veronica Sanz

items.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
items.summary: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field.
items.author: Chenwei Lv

items.title: Polynomial-time classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss
items.summary: Sampling experiments are a leading approach to demonstrating quantum computational advantage, yet their robustness to experimental noise is not completely understood. We develop a common framework for classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss, including pure loss. For Fock-state boson sampling, Gaussian boson sampling with fixed uniform squeezing, and fermion sampling with magic inputs, we obtain polynomial-time sampling at inverse-polynomial total variation error, for any fixed nonzero overall loss rate, and with high probability over Haar-random interferometers. A milder flatness assumption on the ideal output distribution suffices for quasipolynomial-time simulation without Haar randomness. With constant thermal loss per layer, the same flatness assumption gives polynomial-time simulation at logarithmic depth.
items.author: Armando Angrisani, Hela Mhiri

items.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
items.summary: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target. To introduce quantum auxiliary supervision during training, we employ a quantum neural network (QNN) or quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold network (QKAN) as an auxiliary solubility prediction head over shared Transformer representations. The auxiliary prediction loss is jointly optimized with the diffusion objective, allowing quantum auxiliary supervision to influence the learned denoising model. Once trained, protein sequences are generated entirely through classical reverse diffusion. On the CATH benchmark, DiffSequence-Q achieved the highest secondary structure recovery among the four evaluated models for complete sequence generation.

items.title: Study on hydration cementation and enhancement mechanism of grout-rock interface of PVA modified grouting material
items.summary: by Youwei Li, Haoyu Hu, Yujun Zhang, Gui Liu The weakly cemented sandstone aquifer in coal mine is prone to particle softening under mining disturbance and water-rock interaction, which induces the decrease of rock integrity and the development of water conducting channel, leading to the instability and failure of aquifer. To address the low early-age hydration activity of grouts containing a high proportion of coal gangue, discontinuous grout-rock interfacial bonding, and limited adaptability to weakly cemented sandstone, this paper uses cement and coal gangue(CG) as raw materials to prepare modified grouting materials with different polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) content. The uniaxial compression, XRD, FTIR and SEM test methods were used to systematically study the influence of PVA content on the performance of solid waste based slurry, the bearing characteristics of slurry-rock composite, the evolution of hydration products and the interface micro structure.

items.title: An explainable machine learning framework for cross-dataset chronic kidney disease risk prediction using hybrid data balancing
items.summary: by Jarin Tasnim Mumu, Ismail Hossain, Kazi Md. Tanvir Anzum Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health problem, and early detection is important for reducing complications and improving treatment. Machine learning has shown strong potential for CKD prediction, but many existing studies rely on single datasets, face severe class imbalance, and provide limited interpretability. These challenges reduce model reliability and make cross-dataset use in real clinical settings more difficult. Therefore, this study aimed to develop an interpretable and adaptable machine learning framework for CKD risk prediction across different datasets. The proposed hybrid explainable machine learning (HXAI-ML) framework used two public CKD datasets: the UCI CKD Risk Factor Prediction dataset as the source dataset and the Kaggle CKD dataset as the target dataset.

Harpagide, a naturally occurring iridoid glycoside, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities; however, its therapeutic potential in SAE remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods A mouse model of SAE was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 18 mg/kg).

items.title: Unveiling Molecular Basis of Terminalia chebula in Modulating the AGE-RAGE-PRKCB Axis in Diabetic Nephropathy: Integrative Network Pharmacology and Computational Study

Khairul Islam AbstractDiabetic nephropathy (DN), a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes, remains a principal cause of renal failure worldwide, yet its multifaceted molecular complexity continues to challenge effective therapeutic intervention. In this study, an integrative network pharmacology and computational modeling framework was employed to unravel the mechanistic basis of Terminalia chebula in mitigating DN pathology. A total of 357 phytoconstituents were retrieved from the IMPPAT 2.0 and PubChem databases and screened through SwissADME and pkCSM, yielding 14 bioactive, drug-like, and non-toxic compounds. Target prediction integrated data from SwissTargetPrediction, BindingDB, and CTD, while DN-related genes were compiled from GeneCards, OMIM, and transcriptomic datasets (GSE154561, GSE154881, GSE217709, and GSE30528).

items.title: PIP5K isoforms and phosphoinositide molecular species in EGF-stimulated PIP 3 synthesis: A multi-method approach using enzyme genetic suppression and chemical inhibition in MCF10A cells
items.summary: by Iosif Alexandrou, Vikki Flemington, Martin E. Swarbrick, Sabina Cosulich, Phillip T. Hawkins, Len R. Stephens The membrane phospholipid PI(4,5)P 2 has structural functions and is a substrate for PLC and PI3K enzymes to generate Ins(1,4,5)P 3 , DAG and PI(3,4,5)P 3 signals. PIP5Ks, that 5-phosphorylate PI4P, are the major source of PI(4,5)P 2 in mammalian cells. Current thinking suggests distinct pools of PI(4,5)P 2 may be differentially generated by PIP5Kα, β and γ isoforms and involved in different physiological functions. Phosphoinositides are comprised of families of acyl-chain variants but are uniquely enriched in C38:4 species. There is evidence that PIP5Ks are selective for certain acyl chain species of PI(4)P.

items.title: Gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, and patient-reported outcomes in Class III orthognathic surgery patients: An item-level analysis
items.summary: by Gizem Altundal, Asuman Deniz Gümrü Celikel, Gülnaz Marsan Objective To evaluate gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, functional and psychosocial evaluations, and treatment process perceptions among adult patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion undergoing orthodontic preparation for orthognathic surgery. Methods In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 81 adults (37 females, 44 males) with skeletal Class III malocclusion completed a 27-item investigator-developed questionnaire during pre-surgical orthodontic preparation, covering demographics, problem awareness, functional and psychosocial evaluations, motivation and expectations, treatment process, and patient engagement. Gender differences were analyzed item by item with Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, or Fisher’s exact tests. P-values for the 37 comparisons were adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure within questionnaire domains, and effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals were estimated.

items.title: Ecological traits predict extinction risk of the world’s traded carnivores
items.summary: by Erik Joaquín Torres-Romero, Maximilian L. Allen, Vincent Nijman, Moreno Di Marco, Christopher J. O’Bryan, Vincenzo Penteriani Wildlife trade is a major driver of biodiversity loss, yet how trade interacts with species’ ecological traits and extinction risk remains underexplored. Carnivores warrant special attention because they are disproportionately exploited and vulnerable to extinction compared to other taxa. We analyzed 171,637 international trade records spanning 50 years (1975–2024) for 129 carnivore species listed under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). We analyzed trade volumes across the globe and then used logistic regression to evaluate associations between ecological traits and extinction risk, as well as family-level differences in extinction risk.

items.title: Effectiveness of nurse-led hypertension interventions on retention, adherence, and blood pressure control among adults in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review
items.summary: by Tagese Yakob, Charuai Suwanbamrung, Cua Ngoc Le, Abebe Sorsa Badacho, Udomsak Saengow Background Hypertension affects more than 1.28 billion adults globally and remains the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, stroke, renal failure, and premature death. This burden is inconsistently distributed across Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs), where nearly three-quarters of adults live with hypertension. This gap is largely driven by poor adherence and low retention. This systematic review aims to assess the effectiveness of nurse-led interventions on retention in care, medication adherence, and blood pressure among adult patients with hypertension in primary health care settings in LMICs.

items.title: Microclimatic regulation effects of landscape elements on university campus in a temperate monsoon climate zone: A case study during extreme summer heat
items.summary: by Lei Fan, Yixin Liang, Zixian Li, Yan Zhou Although temperate monsoon climate regions are traditionally known for their harsh winter climates, the combined effects of rapid urbanization and global climate change have significantly intensified summer urban heat island effects in these areas, making them a neglected yet increasingly severe challenge in high-latitude urban climate adaptation planning. This study takes a typical campus in Shenyang, a temperate monsoon climate region in Northeast China, as the experimental subject. It quantitatively dissects the non-linear statistical associations and regulatory mechanisms of biotic and abiotic landscape elements and their spatial configurations on microclimate parameters and human thermal comfort (Physiologically Equivalent Temperature, PET) by combining microclimate field observations with validated ENVI-met numerical simulations.

items.title: Fabrication and evaluation of a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel for the treatment of ocular bacterial infections
items.summary: by Neda Sistani Karampour, Pouya Dolati, Anayatollah Salim, Maryam Abedini Baghbadorani, Maryam Keykhaee, Somayeh Handali, Eskandar Moghimipour Topical ocular drug delivery is often restricted by rapid precorneal clearance, which can decrease drug residence time and bioavailability at the ocular surface. The purpose of the study was to develop a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel (SA-Nio-Gel) to enhance ocular drug delivery. Thin film hydration method was used for the preparation of SA niosomes, employing nonionic surfactants (Span 60 and Span 80) and cholesterol. The optimized niosomal formulation was then incorporated into a Carbopol 934 gel base to prepare the final SA-Nio-Gel formulation. The optimized niosomes exhibited encapsulation efficiency of 76% ± 1.5 and a mean particle size of 129.7 ± 2.52 nm.

items.title: Ensemble frequency ratio-maximum entropy landslide susceptibility modelling for climate‑resilient road corridors in Bocas del Toro and Chiriquí, Panama
items.summary: by Dereck Mbeh Petiangma, Gerald G. Singh, Enrique Williams, Jeffrey Gerardo Ramos Perez, Rachel Collin Landslides are a major rainfall-triggered hazard affecting road infrastructure across the mountainous terrain of western Panama. This study develops an ensemble Frequency Ratio (FR)-Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) modelling framework to assess landslide susceptibility, identify critical management zones, and determine key drivers of slope failure along road corridors in the mainland districts of Bocas del Toro and along the Rambala-Hornito-David route. Social jetlag, the absolute difference between weekday and weekend sleep midpoints, was categorized as Results Among 4,483 participants, 267 (6.0%) had social jetlag ≥2 h.

items.title: Land degradation neutrality state and progress in the Central Region, Malawi
items.summary: by Kennedy Sones Nazombe, Charles Bakolo, Brighton A. Chunga, Principal Mdolo, Jean Mtethiwa, Rodrick Mlewa, Kennedy Adamson, Devie Chilonga, Kelvin Chomanika Achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) is vital for the long-term sustainability of human well-being and the realisation of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.3.1. We estimated the overall indicator of SDG 15.3.1, the proportion of land that is degraded over the total land area in the Central Region, Malawi, from 2001 to 2022, using the Trends.Earth tool in QGIS. The study applied the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) Good Practice Guidance methodology for SDG Indicator 15.3.1 assessment, integrating land cover, land productivity, and soil organic carbon (SOC) sub-indicators.

items.title: A lightweight vision-based framework for automated aero-engine blade damage inspection
items.summary: by Xiaobo Ning, Hang Zhao, Kang Zeng, Zhengwei Zhang Automated visual inspection of aero-engine blades is central to aviation safety, yet it is challenged by damage that is small and low-contrast against a strongly textured metal surface, and by the need for models that are light enough for edge deployment. This paper presents a lightweight vision-based framework for automated blade damage inspection. Rather than assembling independent detection modules, the framework is organized as a three-stage inspection pipeline: (1) a multi-scale feature-discrimination stage (MSBlock) captures defects across a wide size range at negligible computational cost; (2) a texture-suppression stage (TSA) filters high-frequency machining-background noise through product-based channel–spatial attention, exposing genuine defects; and (3) an efficient-prediction stage (Detect_Efficient) fuses cross-scale features and recalibrates confidence with roughly half the parameters of a standard head.
items.author: Xiaobo Ning, Hang Zhao, Kang Zeng et al.

items.title: Modeling and controlling a half-car model suspension system using an ANFIS controller
items.summary: by Sisay Ewunetie Fisha, Amanuel Gebisa Aga, Tatek Mamo Wachamo Passive suspension systems (PSS) use fixed spring and damping characteristics and cannot adapt to changing road disturbances and operating conditions. Active suspension systems (ASS) address this limitation by generating additional control forces, but controller design must balance ride comfort, road holding, model uncertainty, and control effort. This study develops a four-degree-of-freedom (4-DOF) longitudinal half-car model and evaluates an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controller against PSS and PID-controlled ASS under double-bump and ISO-classified random Type A and Type C Road profiles at 10 and 20 m/s. The ANFIS controller is trained using PID-generated input-output data with two inputs, five Gaussian membership functions per input, 25 Takagi-Sugeno rules, and 150 training epochs.

items.summary: by Julie Cowie, Rhonda Archibald, Scott Findlay, Danielle Hutcheon, Sinéad Currie, Louise Hay, Elizabeth Cook People who are unable to achieve a healthy lifestyle are at greater risk of type II diabetes, some cancers, heart disease, stroke, mobility problems and poor outcomes from disease. For individuals living in disadvantaged areas, life circumstances such as low income, unemployment, working anti-social hours and limited local services present barriers to the challenge of living healthy lives. Working with two disadvantaged communities in Forth Valley, Scotland, we co-designed and implemented an evidence-informed, incentive-based intervention, Enjoy Life LocallY (ELLY), to support citizens with healthy weight and wellbeing.

items.title: Perceived importance, self-rated performance satisfaction, learning stress, and practicum experiences among nursing students: A cross-sectional study with supplementary open-ended responses
items.summary: by Hsiu-Wen Tsai, Shu-Ching Chen This cross-sectional study examined nursing students’ perceived importance and self-rated performance satisfaction regarding fundamental nursing practicum competencies, explored learning-stress scores across academic-achievement categories and psychological-counseling history, and descriptively summarized written practicum experiences. All 730 eligible third-year nursing students were invited; 28 did not participate, 702 returned signed consent forms and questionnaires, and 3 incomplete questionnaires were excluded, leaving 699 participants. Paired importance–performance gaps and 95% confidence intervals were calculated, and 5,000 bootstrap samples assessed coordinate uncertainty and quadrant stability. items.title: Multi-Probe Cosmological Constraints on Clustering DBI Dark Energy Scenario
items.summary: We present a multi-probe observational analysis of a clustering tachyonic Dirac-Born-Infeld~(DBI) dark energy model. Its noncanonical kinetic term gives a subluminal sound speed, so dark energy perturbations can grow on subhorizon scales. Working in a multifluid framework that tracks both the background expansion and linear perturbations, we constrain the model with nested sampling, using Planck 2018 compressed CMB distance priors, DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, $fσ_8$ growth data, and three Type Ia supernova compilations: Pantheon$+$, DES-SN5YR, and Union3. The standard cosmological parameters agree with $Λ$CDM within $2σ$, with DBI preferring a slightly lower $H_0$ and higher $Ω_{m0}$, with the largest shift being $\simeq1.8σ$ in $H_0$ for Pantheon$+$.

items.title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
items.summary: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|α\rangle$. We demonstrate that single-photon-added coherent states (SPACS) generated via coherent seeding possess a quantum relative entropy that precisely quantifies the entanglement deficit between signal and idler fields.

items.title: Crosstalk-Induced Row Hammer Attacks on Quantum Random Access Codes
items.summary: Quantum processors remain susceptible to crosstalk-induced effects despite the continuous evolution of their underlying hardware architectures. In this work, we experimentally investigate the effectiveness of crosstalk-induced attacks across six IBM superconducting quantum processors and one IQM processor. Our results demonstrate that such attacks can be launched across all the platforms, due to persistance of crosstalk, although their effectiveness varies significantly between devices. The probability of a measurement outcome flip in the victim qubits reaches a maximum value of $60\%$. Also, it is seen that processors sharing identical coupling graphs exhibit different vulnerability profiles, indicating that connectivity alone is insufficient to predict attack efficiency.

items.title: Autler-townes energy-level engineering for high-quality all-microwave qubit gate
items.summary: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing, yet existing approaches are limited: frequency-tuning techniques induce decoherence, while all-microwave-driven schemes suffer the trade-off between gate speed and leakage rate. Here, we introduce an energy-level engineering technique that employs the Autler-Townes effect to manipulate the nonlinearity of qubits without perturbing the computational subspace or degrading coherence time. This approach enables an experimentally validated, fast (97 ns) and high-fidelity (99.40(9)%) CZ gate, where error analysis reveals that gate errors arise mainly from static decoherence. The scheme facilitates fast, high-quality all-microwave gate operations with a simple topology and can be applied across various quantum platforms.

items.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
items.summary: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model.

items.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
items.summary: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $ξ$-attractors, in which a single function $f(φ)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(φ)$ which is $f'(φ)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(φ)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate.

items.title: Negative non-linear differential dissipation in mechanical quartz resonators
items.summary: We observe negative non-linear differential dissipation in a low-frequency (32.7 kHz) miniature quartz tuning fork, representing a high-Q piezoelectric resonator, at temperatures below 0.3 K. Similar drive-induced dissipation suppression has previously been reported in superconducting microwave resonators, and high-frequency MEMS devices, associated to coupling with tunneling two-level systems (TTLSs). In the case of low-frequency resonators, the equivalent temperature of the mechanical mode is orders of magnitude lower than the thermodynamic temperature of the device, implying that accessible TTLS states are largely saturated. We demonstrate that the observed temperature and drive dependence of the losses fit well within the framework of an interacting TTLS bath, indicating the presence of a channel for energy transfer between the mechanical mode and thermally activated TTLSs.

items.title: Learning complex temporal dependencies via local synaptic plasticity
items.summary: The ability to extract and exploit temporal structure across diverse tasks is central to human cognition. Neuroscientists have typically relied on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT) when modelling neural and behavioural processes such as decision-making and motor control. However, this algorithm has limited biological plausibility, hence the computational principles underlying efficient learning of temporal dependencies remain unresolved. Here, we investigate temporal predictive coding (tPC), a recently proposed framework that extends predictive coding to the temporal domain while preserving local Hebbian update rules. We analyse and extend tPC to establish its relationship with several influential computational models of learning in RNNs, including BPTT, reservoir computing, and eligibility propagation (e-prop).

Immediate early response 3 (IER3) is a stress-responsive protein involved in cell survival, but its role in cutaneous fibrosis remains unclear. We investigated the functional significance of IER3 in dermal fibroblasts and its potential contribution to fibrosis. Methods: IER3 expression was examined in skin samples from patients with systemic sclerosis, keloids, and hypertrophic scars. Primary human dermal fibroblasts were stimulated with transforming growth factor-{beta}1 (TGF-{beta}1). RNA sequencing, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, quantitative PCR, and flow cytometric apoptosis assays were performed to investigate the downstream mechanisms and functional consequences of IER3 expression.

items.title: Lac1-dependent ceramide synthesis couples septum assembly to cell separation in Schizosaccharomyces pombe
items.summary: Ceramides are precursors of complex sphingolipids and bioactive membrane lipids. In the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe, they are produced by a ceramide synthase with two catalytic subunits, Lac1 and Lag1, which are redundant but not functionally equivalent: only Lac1 is required for normal growth and cell size. Why Lac1 has this unique role, and how ceramide synthesis contributes to cell morphogenesis, remain unknown. Here, we show that Lac1 couples septum assembly to cell separation. Cells lacking Lac1 die predominantly during cell separation and build septa with a thinner primary layer and markedly thicker secondary layers, accompanied by altered deposition of {beta}-(1,3)-glucans and galactomannan.

items.title: Optimizing the efficiency of assisted reproduction procedures in the common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus) improved IVF outcomes
items.summary: The marmoset has emerged as a model species for genetic studies of complex neurodevelopmental conditions because of their brain development, behavior, communication, and compact size. IVF has been used to generate wild-type and transgenic marmoset embryos, but inefficiency of IVF in the marmoset compared to other primates poses challenges for genetic manipulation. To address this limitation, we analyzed the association between variables of age, number of cycles, and progesterone levels for IVF and embryology outcomes. Longitudinal data collected over 2 years indicated that the progesterone levels 24 hours after Cloprostenol sodium (Estrumate) administration, the number of days of ovarian stimulation during an IVF cycle, and the number of oocyte retrievals that an animal had undergone all influenced IVF cycle outcomes.

items.title: Combined elevated temperature and CO2 alter Wolbachia abundance and host fitness but not cytoplasmic incompatibility in a stored-product pest
items.summary: Coinfecting endosymbiont strains may respond differently to environmental change, with consequences for host performance and reproductive incompatibility. We investigated an isofemale line of Callosobruchus chinensis coinfected with the cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI)-inducing Wolbachia strains wBruCon (Con) and wBruOri (Ori), together with derived Con-only and uninfected sublines. Beetles were maintained under control conditions (30{degrees}C, ~500 ppm CO2) or under combined elevated temperature and CO2 (32{degrees}C, ~1000 ppm CO2; eT&CO2). In coinfected adults, Ori relative abundance declined under eT&CO2, whereas Con abundance increased in females. Con responses also depended on host sex and infection status, with singly infected males showing particularly high abundance under control conditions.
items.author: San, P. P., Fujita, R., Ferrari, J. et al.

items.title: Intensive pine plantation management shapes infectious agent communities in the generalist rodent Apodemus sylvaticus, with consequences for zoonotic hazard
items.summary: Land use change is widely recognized as a major driver of emerging zoonotic diseases. Yet, while forest plantations are expanding worldwide, their consequences on the circulation of infectious agents in wildlife remain poorly understood. We investigated how native pine plantations and broadleaved habitats shape rodent-associated infectious hazard in the generalist wood mouse (Apodemus sylvaticus), in southwestern France. Using a multi-season survey, we screened 424 wood mice for a broad range of infectious taxa and compared infection probability and infected-host abundance among pine plantation edges, broadleaved hedgerows embedded within pine plantations and broadleaved forests. Using a combination of linear mixed model and joint species distribution modelling, we tested whether infectious hazard differed between pine plantations and broadleaved forests, whether broadleaved hedgerows shifted these patterns towards those observed in broadleaved forests, and how these habitat-related patterns varied across seasons.
items.author: Berard, A., Galan, M., Pradel, J. et al.

items.title: Concrete waste as a source of calcium and alkalinity for coccolithophore cultivation: an experimental test of carbon dioxide removal and sequestration
items.summary: Cultivation of calcifying microalgae has been proposed as a route to carbon dioxide removal (CDR), but biogenic calcification releases CO2 unless the calcium supplied also adds alkalinity. We used cultures of the coccolithophore Chrysotila sp to test whether hydrated lime (Ca(OH)2), supplied as a reagent or within ground waste concrete, can provide both calcium and alkalinity. In a 26-day factorial batch experiment, we monitored pH, nitrate and dissolved calcium. Calcite was quantified by thermogravimetric analysis. Nitrate concentration decreased and calcite accumulated in all algal treatments, indicating that lime or concrete did not inhibit growth or calcification. Lime and concrete raised culture pH significantly whereas the algal growth rate inferred from nitrate drawdown did not differ among treatments.
items.author: Ferriere, M., Affholder, A., Welchert, J. et al.

items.title: Interactive effects of Nutrient Enrichment and Water Scarcity on Floral signaling and visitation
items.summary: - Floral traits remain an underexplored frontier in global change biology compared to their vegetative counterparts. As anthropogenic change involves simultaneous shifts in resource availability, focusing on isolated stressors may overlook complex biological responses. Characterizing the interactive effects of these stressors is therefore crucial to move beyond additive models and accurately predict the stability of pollination services in a transforming world. - The individual and interactive effects of nutrient enrichment and water scarcity were investigated on the floral traits and pollinator visitation rates of five grassland species. - While species identity emerged as the dominant driver of overall trait variation, across-species responses were also present.
items.author: Manavalan, M., Thakur, D., Panthi, B. et al.

items.title: Human senataxin uses distinct peripheral elements to unwind R-loops and act on RNA polymerase II
items.summary: Persistent R-loops and paused or stalled RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) elongation complexes can threaten genome stability. Senataxin (SETX) contributes to R-loop resolution and RNAPII regulation, but their intimate connection during transcription makes the individual contributions of these activities difficult to distinguish in cells. To determine whether these activities rely on the same molecular features, we investigated the structure and biochemical properties of the SETX helicase domain (SETX-HD). Cryo-EM defines the conserved helicase core and RNA-binding channel of SETX-HD, while biochemical analyses identify distinct roles for two peripheral elements: a previously uncharacterised C-terminal RNA-binding domain (CT-RBD) and the prong subdomain. In reconstituted mammalian transcription assays, SETX-HD promotes passage beyond a defined RNAPII pause and elongation-complex dissociation on the same template.
items.author: Lanicek, M., Sedova, K., Hasanova, Z. et al.

items.title: N-GLYcanyzer monitoring of a microperfusion process reveals critical parameters' impact on Trastuzumab biosimilar N-glycoform time evolution
items.summary: Controlling monoclonal antibody (mAb) N-glycosylation as a critical quality attribute (CQA) remains challenging in continuous and intensified biomanufacturing, where conventional end-point analyses obscure dynamic pathway responses. Here, we deployed the N-GLYcanyzer process analytical technology (PAT) for automated monitoring of a microperfusion process that reveals critical parameters' impact on Trastuzumab biosimilar N-glycoform time evolution across a 20-day culture duration of Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells in a ~2 mL scale-down microbioreactor perfusion platform. Using offline PAT assays combined with our integrated at-line PAT workflow, we systematically screened six perfusion process parameters: carbon source, viable cell density (VCD), perfusion rate, temperature, and pH.
items.author: Narvekar, A., Harrison, M., Thakur, R. et al.

items.title: A compact motif vocabulary is differentially interpreted across human cell types
items.summary: How a common genome generates diverse human cell types may depend less on distinct cis-regulatory vocabularies than on context-dependent use of a shared one. We have developed CNN-CR, an interpretable neural network that learns regulatory motifs while predicting gene expression across 116 human biosamples. Promoter regulation proves highly compressible: dozens of recurrent motif families retain most of the predictive information of much larger cell-type-specific vocabularies and generalize to cellular contexts excluded from their discovery. These motifs are conserved at their binding sites and enriched at fine-mapped regulatory variants. Cellular context acts at two levels: chromatin state gates which motif instances are available for regulatory use, whereas reader identity determines how accessible motifs are interpreted.
items.author: Shen, S., Wang, W.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Protein Language Models for Dual-Target Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery Under Strict Homology Constraints
items.summary: The worldwide escalation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a severe challenge to modern public health, necessitating novel classes of therapeutic agents. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent highly promising alternatives to small-molecule antibiotics due to their co-evolutionary resilience and rapid membrane disruption dynamics. However, translating computational AMP leads into clinical drug candidates remains bottlenecked by off-target cytotoxicity, predominantly hemolytic activity against mammalian erythrocytes. Although pretrained foundational protein language models (PLMs) have rapidly advanced molecular property prediction, current architectures frequently isolate antibacterial potency and cytotoxicity into disconnected single-task pipelines or succumb to catastrophic performance drops under strict homology-controlled evaluations. Recently, the Quantitative Mapping of Antimicrobial Peptides (QMAP) benchmark proposed that frozen PLM embeddings show weak linearly accessible features for hemolytic activity (HC50) resulting in poor rank correlation ({rho} < 0.25) on out-of-distribution sequence splits.
items.author: Jat, R., Ejaz, S. R.

items.title: Redesigning the Eterna100 RNA design benchmark for the Vienna 2 folding engine
items.summary: The rational design of RNA is becoming important for rapidly developing technologies in medicine and biochemistry, spurring development of numerous RNA secondary structure design algorithms and benchmarks to evaluate their performance. However, the problem of RNA design is dependent upon the inverse problem of RNA structure prediction through "folding engines" that predict structure from sequence. We hypothesized that differences in RNA folding engines could impact design algorithms, and recruited an online community of RNA design experts to modify the widely used RNA secondary structure design benchmark Eterna100 to address target unsolvability when changing the folding engine used (ViennaRNA 1 updated to 2).
items.author: Koodli, R. V., Rudolfs, B., Romano, J. et al.

items.title: Single-cell characterization of 3D CLL spheroid model that recapitulates lymph node microenvironment-driven phenotypes and in vivo drug responses to ibrutinib
items.summary: Lymph node (LN) microenvironmental signals promote chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) cell survival, proliferation, and treatment resistance. We previously developed a 3D culture model that recapitulates key features of this protective LN niche. Using single-cell RNA sequencing of ex vivo paired peripheral blood and LN samples, together with matched patient-derived CLL spheroids, we investigated how microenvironmental cues shape CLL phenotypes and their response to ibrutinib. A total of 3 functional CLL states (resting, activated, proliferating) were identified, with expanded populations of activated and proliferating subsets in 3D cultures. After 5 days of in vitro ibrutinib treatment, CLL cells shifted toward a resting phenotype, reflecting published responses in patients at 6 months.
items.author: Haselager, M. V., Lashgari, D., Jongejan, A. et al.

items.title: Polycomb Marked Promoter Methylation Gains in Aging and Cancer are Independent of Replication
items.summary: DNA methylation alterations are hallmark features of aging and cancer, occurring early during tumor initiation. Yet how these changes evolve during early tumorigenesis, and whether oncogenic signaling actively drives them, remains poorly understood due to limitations in resolving this at the longitudinal and clonal level. Here we developed a genome-wide DNA methylation profiling method for low DNA amounts and applied it to single stem cell-derived clones from a BRAFV600E -inducible mouse colon organoid model, tracking nucleotide-level methylation heterogeneity over time. BRAFV600E induction produced stepwise methylation divergence consistent with progressive clonal takeover, in contrast to gradual epigenetic drift in uninduced controls.
items.author: Easwaran, H., Thursby, S.-J., Patel, N. et al.

items.title: ORTHOTOPIC TUMOUR INDUCTION PROTOCOL SHAPES TUMOUR MICROENVIRONMENT
items.summary: Robust preclinical cancer models are essential for studying tumour progression and evaluating therapeutic strategies. Orthotopic implantation of tumour cells into the mammary gland is widely used to model triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet substantial variation exists in the number of cells used to initiate tumours, often without explicit consideration of how this parameter shapes tumour biology. Here, we systematically assess how tumour cell number at implantation influences the tumour microenvironment using the 4T1 orthotopic TNBC model. Mammary tumours initiated with different cell numbers exhibited comparable early growth kinetics and gross size, yet diverged markedly in cellular density, hypoxia, necrosis, proliferation, vascular integrity, and immune cell infiltration.
items.author: McClelland, S., Liu, Y., Allocca, G. et al.

items.title: IDENTIFICATION OF CANDIDATE GENES UNDERLYING A NOVEL QTL FOR ROOT LENGTH AND DIAMETER IN BARLEY IN RESPONSE TO SALINITY
items.summary: Salinity is a major agricultural problem that decreases growth and yield of crops and is expected to worsen with climate change. Improving salt tolerance through breeding could be facilitated by identification of genetic loci and candidate genes affecting root traits that enhance water and nutrient uptake while limiting accumulation of toxic ions. In this study, a Clipper x Sahara 3771 doubled haploid (DH) barley mapping population was screened for root growth responses to saline conditions in a controlled environment. Quantitative trait loci (QTLs) were mapped for root traits including seminal root length, root diameter and root potassium. Major QTLs affecting seminal root length and average root diameter were detected in the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 2H, indicating that this region is a key determinant of root architecture under both control and saline conditions.
items.author: Mather, D., Situmorang, A., Brien, C. et al.

items.title: Reduced enteric Bdnf expression and TrkB-dependent regulation of Vip in a Mecp2-null mouse model of Rett syndrome-associated gastrointestinal dysmotility
items.summary: Gastrointestinal (GI) dysmotility is a highly prevalent and clinically significant feature of Rett syndrome (RTT), yet its underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated these mechanisms of GI dysmotility in a Mecp2null mouse model of RTT. First, we observed that MeCP2 was expressed in murine myenteric ganglia, including in enteric neurons and that Mecp2null males developed maturation associated functional regression in their GI motility. In dysmotile mice, longitudinal muscle myenteric plexus tissue showed marked reductions in enteric Bdnf isoforms IV, VI, and II, whereas expression of the BDNF receptor isoforms TrkB.FL and TrkB.T1 was not significantly altered, consistent with reduced enteric BDNF TrkB signaling.
items.author: Puttapaka, S. N., Admasu, I. A., Scott, A. et al.

items.title: Myelin Governs Hippocampal Network Function through the Extracellular Space it Occupies, Not Only the Axons it Insulates
items.summary: Myelin, the multilamellar sheath wrapping neuronal axons, enables saltatory conduction. Beyond electrical insulation, myelin occupies volume, and therefore shapes the extracellular space (ECS) through which interstitial fluid flows and neurotransmitter diffuses. How these two roles interact is unknown. We built a multi-scale model of hippocampal CA1 coupling lattice Boltzmann simulations of ECS flow to detailed networks of reconstructed neurons and glia. Demyelination enlarged the ECS volume fraction from 28 to 43 per cent up to 43 to 70 per cent across layers, lowered tortuosity from about 1.7 to 1.4, raised effective diffusivity from 0.35 to 0.50 of free solution and shortened solute breakthrough times by roughly a third, while raising flow speed yet lowering viscous dissipation.
items.author: Jia, X., Zeng, C., Liu, L. et al.

items.title: Path knockout: an analysis tool for connectome-driven circuit discovery
items.summary: Neural circuits in the brain transform sensory information into perceptual, emotional and motor output. The connectome -- a synaptic-resolution wiring diagram of all neurons in a nervous system -- provides a neuroanatomical blueprint for identifying different circuits that mediate specific computations. However, its sheer scale and complexity pose a significant challenge in extracting functionally relevant multi-synaptic pathways. Here we established path knockout, a connectome analysis method that identifies dominant multi-synaptic pathways. Path knockout uses the input fraction of each synaptic connection as a surrogate for the probability that information transfer succeeds across that synapse and calculates approximate probability, or connection strength, that at least one path succeeds among all multi-synaptic paths between defined source and sink neuron populations.
items.author: McGrath, R., Hattori, D.

items.title: A medial entorhinal connectome reveals compartmentalized microcircuit architecture
items.summary: The medial entorhinal cortex (MEC) transforms multimodal inputs into spatial representations, but the synaptic architecture underlying its computations remains unclear. Here we generated a synapse-resolution connectomic dataset spanning all six layers of mouse MEC and the adjacent parasubiculum with serial electron microscopy, providing a continuous volume for mapping cellular organization and connectivity across layers and regions. We found that clustered pyramidal neurons in MEC layer II extended oblique apical dendrites with a dorsolateral bias and long-range myelinated axons within the layer. Exhaustive reconstruction of one cluster revealed a central exclusion core (ExC) that spatially partitioned basal dendritic architecture and synaptic connectivity.
items.author: Shi, T., Chen, Y., Jin, H. et al.

items.title: Wolffia globosa -derived nanovesicles as a natural source of bioactive metabolites with neuroprotective potential against methylglyoxal-induced oxidative stress
items.summary: Plant-derived nanovesicles (PDNVs) have attracted increasing attention for their potential biomedical applications, particularly in oxidative stress-related diseases and neuroprotection. Wolffia globosa, an emerging functional food and potential future food source, is rich in phytochemicals associated with health-promoting properties. Harnessing W. globosa-derived nanovesicles (WGNVs) represents a promising strategy for expanding the biomedical applications of this plant. In this study, WGNVs were isolated and characterized, and their neuroprotective potential was evaluated in vitro. The isolated WGNVs exhibited nanoscale dimensions and a lipid bilayer structure. Biochemical analyses revealed substantial total phenolic and flavonoid contents, alongside intrinsic antioxidant activities. Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified a diverse repertoire of metabolites, including major constituents subsequently validated using independent analytical approaches.
items.author: Khongkla, E., Boonsnongcheep, P., Srisaisup, M. et al.

items.title: Region-dependent regulation of Tau phosphorylation by Glycerophosphodiester Phosphodiesterase 2 in a mouse model of tauopathy
items.summary: Hyperphosphorylation of Tau promotes its aggregation and neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) formation, contributing to neuronal dysfunction and neurodegeneration in diseases such as Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRDs). However, the mechanisms underlying dysregulated Tau phosphorylation under pathological contexts remain unclear. Glycerophosphodiester phosphodiesterase 2 (GDE2) is a six-transmembrane enzyme that acts at the cell surface to cleave the glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchor that tethers a subclass of proteins to the membrane. Here, we show that in the PS19 tauopathy mouse model, GDE2 disruption modulates Tau phosphorylation by transiently decreasing Tau's propensity for aggregation through region-specific regulation of local kinase environments. In the cortex, GDE2 ablation in 6-month-old PS19 male mice (PS19;Gde2KO) reduces Tau phosphorylation at Serine (S)202/Threonine (T)205, T212, and S396 but increases S262 phosphorylation in the hippocampus of 6-month-old PS19;Gde2KO male and female mice.
items.author: Jimenez-Ornelas, C., Sockanathan, S.

items.title: Dissociable norepinephrine and dopamine representations during strategic decision-making and reward learning
items.summary: Adaptive decision-making in competitive environments requires learning from immediate reward outcomes while tracking longer-timescale information to adjust behavioural strategies and remain unpredictable against others. Dopamine (DA) and norepinephrine (NE) have long been implicated in reward-guided behaviours, but their contributions to strategic choice remain unclear. We trained mice to play a zero-sum matching pennies game against a computer opponent that exploited regularities in their choice and reward history, such that optimal performance required stochastic choice decoupled from immediate reward. We combined fibre photometry recordings, behavioural and neural modelling, and a within-subject multi-task design to determine how NE and DA contribute to strategic choice in the matching pennies game versus reward-guided behaviour in a two-armed bandit (2AB) task.
items.author: Aloor, J., Sit, T. P., Geuter, J. et al.

items.title: Oscillatory Phase Coding Emerges in Adaptive RNNS for Flexible Working Memory
items.summary: Oscillatory phase coding (OPC) is widely observed in neural systems and has been implicated in cognitive functions such as memory and sequence processing. However, its computational role and neural substrates remain largely unclear. Here, we studied OPC by training recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with adaptation to perform sequence working memory tasks with variable delays. After training, we found that OPC emerges in the RNN spontaneously: the memorized items recur at distinct phases of a shared rhythm, with oscillation amplitude encoding item identity and phase encoding serial order. Ablation studies identified three key elements required for OPC: adaptation in neural dynamics, variable delay in memory retention, and flexibility in reading out information.
items.author: Lu, K., Chu, T., TUERHONG, A. et al.

items.title: Biomarkers indicate altered outer retinal fluid homeostasis in the absence of Kv2.1/Kv8.2 channels.
items.summary: Purpose: Photoreceptor Kv2.1/Kv8.2 voltage-gated potassium channels carry an outward potassium current, helping to set the resting membrane potential and to shape dim light responses. Because potassium flux in the outer retina influences extracellular osmolarity and fluid distribution, we hypothesized that Kv2.1/Kv8.2 channels also contribute to fluid homeostasis in this region of the retina. Methods: OCT imaging was performed in Kv8.2 heterozygous (Het) and knockout (KO) mice aged ~5 weeks under dark- and light-adapted conditions. Light-dark differences in the distance between the external limiting membrane (ELM) and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) ({Delta}ELM-RPE) were calculated to quantify light-evoked outer retinal expansion, a biomarker associated with changes in subretinal space (SRS) fluid handling.
items.author: Laird, J. G., Soetedjo, J., Inamdar, S. M. et al.

items.title: Integrated metabolomics and proteomics from voxelated cortical hemispheres of adult rhesus monkeys
items.summary: The spatial organization of molecular networks across cortex likely contributes to differences in local circuit vulnerability in aging and Alzheimer's disease; yet many existing molecular datasets sacrifice spatial structure, sampling only a handful of regions per brain. Here, we present a framework for generating spatially registered, paired metabolomic and proteomic maps across an entire cortical hemisphere of an adult rhesus monkey, at millimeter resolution. One hemisphere each from two animals was harvested under controlled conditions, approximately flattened, and hand dissected at different sampling resolutions (roughly 2.5 and 4 mm/side) into tissue voxels. Each voxel was split after homogenization and extraction to provide matched aliquots for targeted metabolomics and deep untargeted proteomics.
items.author: Wu, Q., Brigande, A. M., Lutz, M. W. et al.

items.title: Multi-scale place fields provide a predictive basis for hierarchical control
items.summary: Hippocampal place cells typically exhibit unimodal spatial selectivity in small enclosures, but express multiple, irregularly spaced fields in environments of naturalistic scale. However, existing predictive-map theories of the hippocampus do not scale well to large environments and do not account for these heterogeneous place field characteristics. Here, we introduce the factorised hierarchical successor representation (fHSR), a predictive map that supports hierarchical control using subgoal-directed subroutines. We show that the fHSR allows efficient generalisation across tasks, scaling favourably with environmental size, and it reproduces key statistical and topological characteristics of multi-scale CA1 place cell activity in rats and bats. Analyses of experimental data further confirmed a novel prediction of the fHSR: population firing rates exhibit spatial periodicity with a characteristic wavelength independent of environmental size.
items.author: Yu, C., Maimon, S. R., Rich, P. D. et al.

items.title: Active vision modulates early cortical stages of visual processing: Evidence from MEG and eye-tracking
items.summary: Vision is fundamentally active. Humans and other mammals make several saccadic eye movements per second. This feature of mammalian vision has received increasing interest across the last decades and many behavioural and neurophysiological studies have investigated how the visual system accounts for the effects of self-generated motion (efference copy) in perceptual processing. Still, it is often believed that, besides accounting for the efference copy and for the rhythmic modulation of activity due to perpetual saccade-fixation cycles, active vision does not further modulate neural processing of visual input obtained during periods of fixation. In contrast, using a gaze-contingent trans-saccadic change design with concurrent MEG and eye-tracking data recording from human participants, we find sequential history effects in visual cortices.
items.author: Huber-Huber, C., De Lange, F. P.

items.title: A Reproducible Pre-Transplant γδ T-cell Effector Signature Reveals Immune-Metabolic Programs Associated with Kidney Allograft Rejection
items.summary: Despite optimized immunosuppression, acute kidney transplant rejection affects 10-20% of recipients within the first year, and no reliable pre-transplant molecular test exists to identify patients at high risk, independent of the donor HLA matching. Across three independent cohorts of kidney transplant recipients, profiled by bulk RNA-sequencing with T-cell receptor repertoire analysis, flow cytometry, CyTOF with paired metabolomics, we identified a reproducible depletion of {gamma}{delta} T cells associated with rejection: an elevated {beta}/{gamma}{delta} T cell ratio in two post-transplant, biopsy-matched cohorts, and depletion of specific {gamma}{delta} T effector clusters in a third, longitudinally sampled cohort. In this third cohort, {gamma}{delta} T cell depletion was already present at the pre-transplant baseline in patients who subsequently developed rejection and remained detectable across the transplant course, indicating that it reflects recipient baseline immune biology rather than a consequence of graft injury.
items.author: Kim, S. M., Sur, S., Koser, K. et al.

items.title: Type I IFN autoantibodies in three of seven Europeans with life-threatening Usutu virus infection.
items.summary: We previously reported that two of three patients with severe Usutu virus (USUV) disease carried circulating autoantibodies (auto-Abs) neutralizing type I IFNs (AAN-I-IFN). Here, we studied four additional patients, bringing the total number of European patients with life-threatening USUV infection to seven (Austria, n = 1; France, n = 1; Hungary, n = 4; Italy, n = 1). Three of these patients (all male, aged 43, 77, and 78 years, one French and two Hungarian) had blood auto-Abs neutralizing at least 10 ng/ml IFN-α2 and IFN-ω and at least 1 ng/ml IFN-β. They suffered from meningitis (n = 1), meningoencephalitis (n = 1), or myocarditis (n = 1).

items.title: Patient-Reported Experiences of Long-Term Recovery and Persistent Psychosocial Burden in NMDAR Encephalitis.
items.summary: Background and objectives N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis is a rare autoimmune disorder with severe neuropsychiatric symptoms. Although neurologic recovery is often favorable, emerging evidence shows high prevalence of long-term sequelae affecting quality of life. Most studies rely on standardized assessments, leaving patient-reported experiences underexplored. We examined long-term psychosocial outcomes using a mixed-methods approach integrating patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), neuropsychological testing, and semistructured interviews informed by qualitative findings from SAPIENCE Level 1. Methods Sixty-five patients with NMDAR encephalitis were recruited across 3 centers (Berlin, Barcelona, and Lyon) at a median of 7.3 years postonset. Remote assessment included semistructured interviews, validated PROMs (sleep quality, fatigue, depression, anxiety, and quality of life), and neuropsychological testing.
items.author: Boeken OJ, Patricio V, Duda-Sikula M, Buttard C, Benaiteau M, Erazo L, Easton A, Papi C, Milano C, Kurpas D, Honnorat J, Dalmau JO, Finke C.

items.title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system.
items.summary: Pneumatosis intestinalis (PI) has a wide range of etiologies, and the imaging differentiation between benign and ischemic PI is difficult, leading to a high risk of missed diagnosis. This study systematically summarizes the CT (Computed Tomography) imaging manifestations of PI and constructs an AI (Artificial Intelligence)-assisted diagnostic model that integrates multidimensional features. This study retrospectively collected CT and x-ray data from 612 patients with PI (398 benign and 214 ischemic cases) from three tertiary hospitals, and included an external validation set of 106 cases. Imaging analysis established a five-level PI-CT severity scoring system based on gas morphology, distribution, portal venous gas (PVG), intestinal wall enhancement, mesenteric edema, and ascites.
items.author: Zhang X.

items.title: Gfi1ab-Cebpβ axis promotes eosinophilopoiesis in zebrafish.
items.summary: Eosinophils play essential roles in parasite defense, allergic responses, and tissue homeostasis, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing their development remain incompletely understood. GFI1 is an important regulator of multiple hematopoietic lineages, but its role in eosinophil development is unclear. Using zebrafish as a model, we demonstrate that Gfi1ab promotes eosinophil development, as gfi1ab mutation significantly reduces eosinophil numbers, whereas its overexpression enhances eosinophilopoiesis. This effect is probably eosinophil-specific, as gfi1ab mutation does not significantly affect erythrocyte, neutrophil, or macrophage development. Integrative RNA-Seq and Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-Seq) analyses identify cebpb as a potential downstream target of Gfi1ab. Mechanistically, gfi1ab deficiency reduces cebpb expression, and cebpb overexpression partially rescues the eosinophil defects in gfi1ab -deficient larvae.
items.author: Wen H, Hu Z, Wu M, Peng W, Sun Y, Li J, Lian J, Huang Y, Zhang Y, Li G.

items.title: Associations between psychiatric comorbidity and intensive care unit length of stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality: A retrospective observational study.
items.summary: Aim Psychiatric comorbidities are common among patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU), but findings regarding their impact on clinical outcomes remain inconsistent. Additionally, existing studies have often included patients admitted for suicide attempts or self-harm, leaving insufficient evidence about the independent effects of psychiatric comorbidity on clinical outcomes. To address this gap, this study investigated the independent association of psychiatric comorbidity with ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality among patients admitted to the ICU, excluding those admitted for suicide attempts or self-harm. Methods Of the 2599 patients admitted to the ICU of a university hospital, 2192 were included in the analysis.
items.author: Nakamura T, Momma T, Yoshizawa T, Arai Y, Sasayama D, Mita A, Imamura H, Hashimoto R, Washizuka S.

items.title: Azole resistance among clinical Aspergillus fumigatus species complex isolates in Greece: first detection of TR 46 -mediated resistance and azole-resistant cryptic species.
items.summary: Objectives To assess the prevalence of antifungal resistance among clinical Aspergillus fumigatus species complex (SC) isolates in Greece, focusing on azole resistance and its underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods A total of 249 clinical A. fumigatus SC isolates were collected from geographically distinct centres across Greece. Antifungal susceptibility testing (AFST) was conducted according to EUCAST guidelines. Cryptic species and azole-resistant A. fumigatus (AR Af ) isolates underwent confirmatory molecular identification. AR Af sensu stricto ( SS ) isolates were further analysed by CYP51A gene and promoter sequencing to detect resistance-associated mutations. Results Most isolates (246/249; 99%) were identified as A. fumigatus SS , while three isolates were molecularly identified as A.
items.author: Siopi M, Vargiami M, Beredaki MI, Velegraki A, Zachariadou L, Roilides E, Chamilos G, Antonopoulou S, Skoura L, Alastruey-Izquierdo A, Pournaras S, Meletiadis J.

items.title: Contextualizing a One Health definition of appropriate antimicrobial use.
items.summary: Background and objectives Antimicrobial stewardship initiatives are designed to improve the appropriateness of antimicrobial use and thereby maximize benefits and minimize risks. Currently, there is no shared understanding of appropriate use. Qualitative research with key stakeholders in human and animal health is critical to inform a One Health definition and to support global stewardship efforts. Methods Four qualitative focus groups were held in 2024 with livestock producers, consumers, healthcare professionals and policymakers to examine factors affecting antimicrobial use and stewardship. A thematic analysis methodology informed by grounded theory was adopted, capturing themes as they emerged directly from the data. Results Thematic analysis identified two themes:Structural and economic barriers; in animal health, consumer demand for free-range or antibiotic-free produce conflicted with practical antimicrobial use.
items.author: Schermuly A, Scarborough R, Dowson L, Teoh L, Biezen R, Bailey K, Hur B, McMullan B, Ierano C, Hardefeldt L.

items.title: Amikacin activity against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae without phenotypic aminoglycoside resistance: impact of aminoglycoside-modifying enzyme (AME) gene aac(6')-Ib-cr in vitro and in vivo .
items.summary: Objectives Aminoglycosides are often combined with β-lactams for the treatment of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, but the impact of aminoglycoside-modifying enzyme (AME) genes on treatment efficacy in phenotypically susceptible isolates remains unclear. We evaluated whether aac(6')-Ib-cr , the AME gene with recognized activity against amikacin, attenuates amikacin efficacy in KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae . Methods Thirteen clinical isolates of KPC-producing K. pneumoniae without phenotypic aminoglycoside resistance (amikacin MIC ≤4 mg/L; median 2, range 0.5-3 mg/L) were studied. Three were AME-negative; 10 were AME-positive, carrying aac(6')-Ib-cr , aac(3)-IIa and strA/strB . Amikacin activity was assessed by time-kill assays and a Galleria mellonella survival model, compared with ceftazidime-avibactam.
items.author: Kim J, Seong JE, Lee YJ, Park S, Han M, Lee Y, Lee JA, Kim JH, Ahn JY, Jeong SJ, Ku NS, Yeom JS, Lee H, Choi JY.

items.title: Global burden of chronic kidney disease attributable to hypertension due to high body mass index: projections to 2050.
items.summary: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects approximately 9.1% of the global population, equivalent to approximately 843 million individuals as of 2021, with hypertension (HTN) as a major contributor. High body mass index (BMI) exacerbates HTN-related kidney injury, but the global burden of HTN-related CKD attributable to high BMI remains poorly characterized. Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study for 1990-2021, we estimated attributable deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and the age-standardized disability-adjusted life-year rate (ASDR). Temporal trends were assessed using the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), and a Bayesian age-period-cohort model was used to project rates to 2050.
items.author: Li L, Zhu G, Wang KK, Maimaiti S, Wang S, Lu C.

items.title: Association between pancreatic ectopic fat deposition and QCT-assessed bone mass status in patients with chronic kidney disease: a cross-sectional study.
items.summary: Background Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at increased risk of bone abnormalities. Beyond disturbances in mineral metabolism, ectopic fat deposition may also be associated with skeletal abnormalities in CKD. However, the relationship between pancreatic fat and bone mass status remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between mean pancreatic fat fraction and quantitative computed tomography (QCT)-assessed bone mass status in patients with CKD. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 327 patients with CKD. Vertebral volumetric bone mineral density was measured using QCT to classify bone mass status as normal bone mass, osteopenia, or osteoporosis. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was quantified from CT images.
items.author: Yang J, Wang R, Xue G, Wei J, Wang L.

items.title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
items.summary: Background Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA. Methods This randomized controlled trial enrolled young women with IDA aged 18-25 years, who were randomly assigned to a training group (TG; n = 16) or a non-training group (NTG; n = 17).
items.author: Harrabi MA, Fendri T, Ayed R, Boughattas W, Chaari F, Mezghani I, Kallel C, Rebai H, Turki M, Ayadi F, Sahli S.

items.title: Extended DNA damage-induced G2/M arrests lead to aberrant mitoses through accumulation of securin.
items.summary: The stochastic nature of DNA damage dictates various scenarios of stress survival among different cells. We used time-lapse microscopy to perform single-cell level analyses of yeast populations with double-stranded DNA breaks and nonfunctional telomeres. Activation of the DNA damage signalling resulted in a broad distribution in the duration of G2/M arrests. Strikingly, the longer arrests correlated with aberrant mitoses caused by miscoordination of nuclear division and cytokinesis, leading to cell death. Chk1-dependent phosphorylation of Pds1 (securin), an inhibitor of sister chromatid separation in mitosis, was responsible for this phenomenon. Securin progressively accumulated during G2/M arrests, leading to grossly delayed or missed nuclear divisions.
items.author: Dubenko A, Jnied M, Kotenko O, Makovets S.

items.title: Configurational patterns associated with relatively higher recent home-based exercise behavior among lung transplant recipients: a fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis.
items.summary: Background Home-based exercise supports functional recovery after lung transplantation, yet exercise behavior varies among recipients. Guided by the capability, opportunity, motivation, and behavior (COM-B) model, this study examined configurations associated with relatively higher recent home-based exercise behavior among lung transplant recipients. Methods This cross-sectional study included adult lung transplant recipients within the first year after transplantation at a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang, China. Five COM-B-related conditions were assessed: 6-min walk distance, exercise rehabilitation knowledge, perceived social support, exercise self-efficacy, and exercise automaticity. Recent home-based exercise behavior during the previous 7 days was assessed through structured retrospective interviews and calculated as MET-min/week.
items.author: Zhu Q, Tang L, Lin P, Zeng F, Lan M.

items.title: Associations of fetal growth patterns and growth in the first two years of life: a longitudinal study of a Beijing birth cohort.
items.summary: Background This study aimed to evaluate the association between fetal growth patterns and early childhood growth rate. Methods In total, 6,370 mother-child pairs were included in a birth cohort in Beijing. Fetal biometric parameters were measured at 20-24, 28-32, 33-36 weeks, and at ≥37 weeks of gestation, and infant weight and length were assessed from birth to 24 months of age. Changes in the weight-for-length Z-score (WLZ) from birth to 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, and 24 months of age were used to classify infant growth velocity as slow (change in WLZ 0.67). A group-based trajectory model was used to identify fetal growth patterns.
items.author: Meng X, Li X, Yi L, Xiong X, Zhong S, Wu M, Zhang N, Wu Q.

items.title: Pharmacological treatment of bereavement-related distress: a systematic review.
items.summary: Background: With the recent addition of prolonged grief disorder into diagnostic manuals both in the United States (i.e. DSM-5-TR) and internationally (i.e. ICD-11), interest in pharmacologic treatment for grief has increased. Objective: Here, we review how bereavement-related psychological distress, including treating depression secondary to bereavement, has been addressed pharmacologically and the efficacy of these treatments. Methods: Included studies focused on (1) patients bereaved by any cause, (2) patients suffering from bereavement-related mental health problems, and (3) pharmacotherapy interventions to treat those bereavement-related mental health problems. Six databases (MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, APA PsycInfo, Scopus, and Web of Science) were searched on 1 October 2020, and updated through 18 December 2024.
items.author: LaPlante CD, Saviano SC, Hardt MM, Pain K, Kolla S, Lee C, Maciejewski PK, Russell D, Smid GE, Prigerson HG.

items.title: Psychosocial pathways linking PTSD and DSO symptoms to somatic symptoms among female North Korean defectors.
items.summary: Background: North Korean defectors (NKDs), approximately 72% of whom are female, are a trauma-exposed population in which somatic symptoms are common and culturally patterned. Previous research identified loneliness, perceived discrimination, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and disturbances in self-organization (DSO) symptoms as correlates of somatic symptoms. However, whether loneliness and perceived discrimination account for these relationships remains unclear. Objective: To examine whether loneliness and perceived discrimination mediate the relationship between PTSD/DSO symptoms and somatic symptoms among female NKDs. Methods: This secondary analysis used cross-sectional survey data from 372 female NKDs in South Korea. PTSD and DSO symptom severity were assessed using the International Trauma Questionnaire.
items.author: Kim H, Kim O, Chu SH.
