items.title: Personality structure mediates the impact of childhood adversity on psychopathology in adolescents with personality disorder.
items.summary: Background: Personality disorders (PD) emerge in adolescence, a developmentally vulnerable period notable for emotional instability and high risk-taking behaviour. After decades of reluctance to diagnose PD in adolescence, early diagnosis and intervention are now called for. Patients present with severe psychopathology including heightened suicide risk. It is important to investigate underlying mechanisms for informed treatment planning. Childhood adversities (CA) are thought to play a key role in developing a PD. Objective: We aimed to deepen our understanding of the mechanism linking CA to psychopathology including suicidality in adolescent PD. Method: In 113 adolescents (mean age 15.6 (SD 1.23), 79 patients and 34 healthy controls), PD was dimensionally assessed using the Structured Interview for Personality Organisation, adapted to the adolescent language (STIPO-R-A), which encompasses identity, interpersonal relationships, defence mechanisms and coping strategies, level of aggression, and moral functioning.
items.author: Czernin K, Bründlmayer A, Zeiler M, Bangerl W, Krischer M, Laczkovics C.

items.title: Caregiver-Reported Signs and Symptoms of Autonomic Dysfunction in Koolen-de Vries Syndrome.
items.summary: Objective To evaluate whether autonomic signs and symptoms are overrepresented in people with Koolen-de Vries syndrome (KdVS). Methods In this observational study, individuals with KdVS and their caregivers were recruited at an international advocacy summit and through social media invitations facilitated by the KdVS Foundation. Caregivers of people with KdVS completed the Pediatric Autonomic Symptoms Scale (PASS) questionnaire and were invited to provide anecdotal reports of their experiences with possible autonomic dysfunction. Data were compared with previously published cohorts of healthy controls, individuals with familial dysautonomia (FD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), or nonspecific neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD). Results Thirty-seven individuals with KdVS participated.
items.author: Sahly AN, Rampakakis E, Myers KA.

items.title: Cryptic Presentations of Neurologic Wilson Disease With ATP7B Peptide Assessments.
items.summary: Objectives To illustrate the phenotypic variability in neurologic Wilson disease (NWD) and diagnostic value of ATP7B peptide testing in resolving WD cases. Methods We conducted a case series analysis of 3 individuals with suspected NWD. Clinical presentation, diagnostic workup including traditional biomarkers, genetic testing, and ATP7B peptide quantification by immuno-selected reaction monitoring mass spectrometry were reviewed. Results The 3 patients demonstrated diverse neurologic presentations: (1) an adult with coexisting Parkinson disease and WD, exhibiting parkinsonian features with partial response to dopaminergic therapy; (2) a child with early-onset dystonia and neuropsychiatric symptoms; and (3) an adult initially misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis.

items.title: Reconsidering the Mechanism of Proton Pump Inhibitor-Associated Fundic Gland Polyps: Absence of Re-enlargement during Potassium-Competitive Acid Blocker Therapy.
items.summary: Fundic gland polyps (FGPs) may enlarge during long-term proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy, potentially in association with acid suppression and hypergastrinemia. Potassium-competitive acid blockers (PCABs) provide potent and sustained acid suppression and may induce comparable or greater elevations in serum gastrin levels than PPIs. We report a case of FGPs in which regression was documented after changes in acid-suppressive therapy, with no subsequent re-enlargement during long-term use of PCABs. A woman in her 60s with gastroesophageal reflux disease developed progressive enlargement of FGPs during 7 years of rabeprazole therapy. Rabeprazole was discontinued because of marked redness of the enlarged FGPs and concern for possible bleeding and was replaced with an H2-receptor antagonist.

items.title: Circulating Plasma Adiposomes as a Partial Lipidomic Readout of Matched Subcutaneous Adipose Tissue: Implications for Interorgan Communication.
items.summary: Background Prior studies established adipose-derived extracellular vesicles, or adiposomes, as mediators of interorgan communication with lipidomic signatures linked to cardiometabolic health. Because adiposomes signal to distant organs via the circulation, we examined whether circulating adiposome lipidomes reflect matched subcutaneous adipose tissue adiposomes. Methods This cross-sectional paired lipidomic study included 22 subjects with matched circulating and subcutaneous adipose tissue adiposome samples. Untargeted lipidomics quantified 773 lipid features across 18 detected broad classes. Spearman correlation was the primary across-subject species-level metric; pooled and within-subject Pearson and Spearman correlations, principal component analysis, Bland-Altman analysis, class composition, and matched-versus-mismatched similarity were complementary measures. Additional analyses evaluated sex, cardiometabolic phenotypes, and focused species-clinical associations.

items.summary: Objective The objective of this research is to design and test a framework for secure monitoring of a vaccine cold-chain with the help of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, blockchain-based provenance verification, and predictive analytics. items.title: Surgical Management of Pediatric Nodular Lymphocyte-Predominant Hodgkin's Lymphoma: A Systematic Review of Surgical Outcomes and Case Report.
items.summary: Introduction Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) is a rare subtype, representing 5% of Hodgkin lymphoma cases. It is distinguished by lymphocyte-predominant cells expressing CD20 and CD79a but not CD15 and CD30. Pediatric NLPHL affects primarily males aged 4-17, often presenting with localized lymphadenopathy and favorable outcomes. NLPHL's distinct pathology makes treatment optimization critical. Long-term risks of chemotherapy and radiotherapy have led to interest in surgical resection for low-risk, early-stage disease. The objective of this study is to systematically review the available literature describing surgical management of pediatric NLPHL and summarize reported outcomes following surgical resection. Methods We conducted a systematic review of studies on pediatric NLPHL with a focus on surgical resection.

items.summary: This work describes, to our knowledge, the first reported case of a patient with an MDS/MPN overlap syndrome harboring a novel KRAS::ETNK1 fusion transcript. The disease initially presented with eosinophilia, megakaryocyte expansion, mast cell infiltration, and a background of typical MDS/MPN-associated mutations ( ASXL1 , TET2 , EZH2 , BCOR , and SETBP1 ). Following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, the fusion-bearing clone disappeared due to a chromosome 12p deletion, and the disease evolved into secondary AML with distinct molecular drivers (MYB, EP300, FAT1, and GATA2). This case provides new insights into rare genetic alterations in MDS/MPN, possible mechanisms of immune-mediated clonal selection after allogeneic stem cell transplantation, and the dynamics of leukemic evolution.

items.title: From ER and mitochondria to contact sites: integrated regulation of ferroptosis in cardiovascular diseases.
items.summary: Iron is a central regulator of cellular redox homeostasis, supporting essential physiological processes. Given its critical biological importance, iron homeostasis is tightly regulated at both the systemic and cellular levels. Ferroptosis is a metabolically regulated, iron-dependent form of cell death characterized by the accumulation of phospholipid hydroperoxides driven by iron-catalyzed redox reactions, ultimately leading to oxidative membrane damage. Accumulating evidence indicates that ferroptosis emerges from the coordinated activity of multiple subcellular organelles rather than from isolated pathways. In this context, the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondria have recently been established as key regulators of ferroptotic signaling. Notably, mitochondria-associated membranes (MAMs), by spatially coordinating redox signaling and lipid peroxidation, calcium fluxes, mitochondrial metabolism and lipid remodeling, are increasingly recognized as central hubs within the ferroptotic cascade, acting as modulators of cellular susceptibility to ferroptosis and as key sites of its execution.

items.title: Differences in genetic diversity between early isolates of yellow fever virus genotypes.
items.summary: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is the prototypical member of the genus Orthoflavivirus and is responsible for the disease yellow fever. Phylogenetic studies show YFV can be characterized into seven genotypes (East Africa [EA], East and Central Africa [ECA], West Africa I [WAI], West Africa II [WAII], South America I [SAI], South America II [SAII], and Angola [ANG]). We used Next Generation Sequencing to investigate and compare the genetic diversity of the seven genotypes of YFV using early isolated strains of known passage history from a variety of collection years. Genetic diversity varied between the seven genotypes, with the ECA genotype being more diverse than EA and WAI genotypes, but not the WAII genotype.

items.title: Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD.
items.summary: Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in type 2 diabetes. Methods This single-center retrospective observational study used prospectively collected peripheral blood monocyte samples from 82 participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD who had received luseogliflozin for at least 6 months. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including FIB-4 index, were evaluated at baseline and 6 months after luseogliflozin initiation.

Methods This single-center retrospective study included 90 patients with type 2 diabetes who had received a GLP-1RA for at least 6 months before switching. items.summary: Introduction High-quality care transitions are essential for sepsis survivors at risk of readmission and long-term complications. These complex innovations require coordination across organizations, individuals, and processes. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) offers a systematic approach to identifying multi-level implementation determinants, but translating them into actionable strategies remains challenging. This study examines the representation of implementation determinants across CFIR domains and visualizes their cross-domain interconnectedness. Methods CFIR-guided, semi-structured pre-implementation needs assessment interviews were conducted with stakeholders involved in sepsis care transitions across five hospital-home healthcare (HHC) dyads. Thirty-two themes identified through deductive-inductive coding were mapped to CFIR domains and constructs and visualized using node diagrams.

items.summary: Introduction Extreme thrombocytosis (EXT; platelet count >1000 × 10 9 /L) is a rare haematological abnormality that may be primary or reactive. We retrospectively evaluated the incidence, management, and complications of EXT in patients with malignancy over a 12-year period. Methods Two-hundred and twenty patients with malignancy experienced at least one episode of EXT during the study period. items.title: Responsible use of new antibiotics for critically ill patients suffering from infections due to carbapenem-resistant organisms-a narrative review for an enablement strategy.
items.summary: Infections caused by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative (MDR-GN) bacteria, particularly carbapenem-resistant organisms (CROs), constitute a significant burden in critically ill patients (CIPs). A multidisciplinary, collaborative approach is essential for responsible antibiotic use in CIPs, balancing the necessity for effective treatment with mitigation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). While the efficacy of existing antibiotics against CROs is increasingly limited due to resistance development and suboptimal pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic properties, several barriers impede the widespread adoption of new agents, including selective susceptibility testing, limited availability, high costs, and concerns regarding the fostering of resistance. Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) strategies aim to optimize antibiotic use; however, there is an ongoing debate between restrictive and enabling approaches for new antibiotics in CIPs with CRO infections.

items.title: DirectClean: artifact-aware preprocessing and read rescue for Oxford Nanopore direct-cDNA transcriptome sequencing.
items.summary: Oxford Nanopore direct-cDNA sequencing enables full-length transcriptome profiling without PCR amplification, but recurrent chimeric artifacts introduced during reverse transcription and library preparation can compromise isoform reconstruction and gene-fusion analysis. These include foldback inversions, aberrant primer configurations, internal adapter concatemers, and homopolymer-mediated template-switching events. Existing preprocessing strategies primarily address primer-based orientation and adapter detection, leaving several direct-cDNA-specific artifact classes unresolved and often discarding reads that still contain usable transcript sequence. We developed DirectClean, an artifact-aware preprocessing and read-rescue framework integrating strand orientation, artifact removal, and junction-level splitting of recoverable chimeric reads. Benchmarking across four direct-cDNA datasets showed consistently higher read and base retention with DirectClean than with Pychopper.

items.title: MHC-II deficiency in a large Algerian cohort: Clinical, immunological, and genetic characterization.
items.summary: MHC class II (MHC-II) deficiency is a rare inborn error of immunity caused by defects in transcriptional regulators of MHC-II expression. In this study, we characterized the clinical, immunological, and molecular features of 107 patients from 98 unrelated Algerian families. Median ages at symptom onset and diagnosis were 5 and 14 mo, respectively, with pneumonia (82%) and chronic diarrhea (73%) predominating. CD4+ T cell lymphopenia occurred in 87.6% and naïve CD4+ T cell depletion in 86.0%. Among 99 genetically characterized patients, variants were identified exclusively in RFXANK (77.8%) and RFXAP (22.2%), including two predominant mutations (RFXANK c.338-25_338del and RFXAP c.368del) and four novel variants.

items.title: Combined Nav1.7-Nav1.8 channel abrogation: Supralinear suppression of excitability in a subpopulation of peripheral sensory neurons.
items.summary: There is a pressing need for nonaddictive pain therapeutics. Despite the genetic validation of peripheral voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels as targets for non-opioid pain therapy, isoform-selective inhibition of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 has yielded limited efficacy in clinical studies, with Nav1.8 blockade providing statistically significant but only partial pain relief. This raises the question: if block of Nav1.8 relieves pain only partially, what is needed for better pain relief? In this study, we utilized dynamic clamp, which permits precisely calibrated functional addition or subtraction of the current from any given channel, to systematically interrogate the combinatorial landscape of multiplex abrogation of currents from Nav1.7 and Nav1.8, both major contributors to electrogenesis within dorsal root ganglion neurons.
items.author: Vasylyev D, Tyagi S, Ghovanloo MR, Zhao P, Waxman SG.

items.title: A transparent window into the rhizosphere: a simplified workflow for spatially resolved soil metabolomics.
items.summary: Root exudates shape nutrient cycling, microbial recruitment, and plant-plant interactions, yet most approaches for analysing exudate chemistry rely on hydroponic systems that poorly represent soil. We present an open-source workflow built around a 3D-printed rhizobox that enables non-destructive root imaging and targeted rhizosphere soil sampling for LC-MS metabolomics. The workflow combines a frame that prints as a single piece on a consumer printer, sampling of defined soil zones registered to root images, and a blank-informed, feature-specific background filter. The filter is essential because ∼90% of detected features also occur in soil, material or solvent controls. In a validation experiment with Arabidopsis thaliana and Phragmites australis , both species grew along the window, and species identity explained 38% of compositional variation among rhizoboxes, whereas sampling date and depth had no detectable effect.
items.author: Subrahmaniam HJ, Moritz P, Becker PJ, Riedner M, Thomsen S, Meier IC, Jensen K.

items.title: Exploring the Transcriptional Responses of Wheat to Sowing Density and Cultivar Mixtures.
items.summary: Cultivar mixtures enhance diversity in fields, offering multiple agronomic benefits while remaining compatible with mechanized agriculture. However, mechanization introduces limitations, such as sowing density, which can influence crop yield. In order to assess the impact of agricultural practices on the plant physiological state, targeted gene expression analysis provides a useful approach. The molecular responses of crops to sowing density and varietal mixtures, particularly in wheat, remain poorly explored. In this study, we examined the transcriptional responses of two binary mixtures of wheat cultivars grown at two sowing densities over two years in semi-controlled mesocosm conditions, using RT-qPCR. Despite notable year-to-year variation in gene expression, consistent transcriptional trends were identified.
items.author: Mathieu L, Chloup A, Gicquelet L, Savajols J, Roumet P, Morel JB, Ecarnot M, Ballini E.

items.title: Change-of-function fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 mutations causing skeletal dysplasias.
items.summary: Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) is a membrane protein that plays a critical role as a negative regulator in the growth and development of the skeletal system. Mutations in FGFR3 cause a range of skeletal dysplasias. The G380R mutation in FGFR3 causes achondroplasia (ACH), the most common form of human short-limbed dwarfism, whereas the A391E mutation in FGFR3 causes Crouzon syndrome, a craniosynostosis characterized by premature fusion of sutures between the cranial bones, with acanthosis nigricans. Both mutations are considered "gain-of-function" and occur close to each other within the simple FGFR3 helix that spans the membrane. Yet, the two pathological phenotypes of ACH and Crouzon syndrome are distinctly different.

items.title: Cold Plasma-Mediated Seed Priming: Plant Stress Responses and Potential Ecological Implications.
items.summary: Cold plasma (CP) is being investigated as a non-thermal seed treatment because studies have reported effects on germination, early seedling growth, plant responses to stress, and seed-borne microorganisms. These effects have been linked to the generation of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS and RNS), changes in seed-surface characteristics, and alterations in physiological and biochemical processes within the plant. However, the response to treatment is not always consistent. It depends on factors such as plant species, plasma source, exposure time, and treatment intensity, while excessive exposure may adversely affect seed performance. Research to date suggests that CP may help improve crop establishment and modify plant responses to biotic and abiotic stresses.

items.title: Electroconvulsive therapy for trunk and visceral cenesthopathy associated with major depressive disorder: A case series of three elderly women.
items.summary: Background Severe cenesthopathy associated with major depressive disorder (MDD) may cause malnutrition and functional decline. We report three elderly women with trunk and visceral cenesthopathy associated with MDD who improved markedly following electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). Case presentation Case A: A woman in her 60s developed MDD while caring for her mother with dementia. Despite pharmacological treatment, trunk, limb, and oral cenesthopathy developed 6 months later, resulting in reduced food intake and physical deterioration. Symptoms improved after six ECT sessions, nearly resolved after 12, and ECT was completed after 15 sessions without recurrence. Case B: A woman in her 70s developed MDD after prolonged caregiving stress.

items.title: An In Vitro Study Simulating Prophylactic Anticoagulation in Haemophilia A and B.
items.summary: Introduction Patients with haemophilia A (HA) and haemophilia B (HB) are at increased bleeding risk. A recent guidance document suggests considering pharmacological thromboprophylaxis on a case-by-case basis in these patients undergoing surgery at high-risk of venous thromboembolism. This study aimed to assess the effect of prophylactic doses of three anticoagulants (enoxaparin, rivaroxaban and unfractionated heparin [UFH]) on in vitro models of HA and HB. Methods FVIII- and FIX-deficient plasma were spiked with FVIII and FIX concentrates to mimic severe, moderate and mild HA (FVIII concentrations Results The PT was not significantly affected by the anticoagulants. A significant prolongation of the APTT was observed; UFH showed the greatest increase, followed by rivaroxaban and enoxaparin.

items.title: Brain and Cardiometabolic Effects of Major Weight Loss in People With Obesity: Preliminary Cohort Findings.
items.summary: Objective Given the overlap between obesity-related metabolic and vascular abnormalities and Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk factors, it is critical to determine whether weight loss improves brain and cardiovascular health. This study examined whether ≥ 40% excess-weight loss is associated with improvements in cardiometabolic risk, brain structure, and cognition. Methods The study was a longitudinal study of individuals with obesity undergoing metabolic and bariatric surgery or medical/behavioral weight-loss treatment. Participants were classified at follow-up as weight-loss (WL; ≥ 40% excess-weight loss) or non-weight-loss (nWL; Results At 1 year, the WL group exhibited improvements in BMI, HbA1C, inflammatory, metabolic, and lipid profiles.

items.title: Inflammation factors mediate association of muscle mass and erectile dysfunction: NHANES 2001-2004.
items.summary: Background Erectile dysfunction (ED) constitutes a global male health issue. Current evidence indicates that low muscle mass may exacerbate insulin resistance and vascular endothelial damage via inflammatory cascades, both of which are established determinants of ED. The relationship between muscle distribution and its effect on ED remains unclear. Aim This study aimed to examine the association between muscle mass and ED prevalence and evaluate potential mediation by inflammatory biomarkers. Methods The study analyzed data from 2217 participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Appendicular lean mass (ALM) is the total lean mass of the limbs. The Appendicular Skeletal Mass Index (ASMI) is calculated as ALM divided by height in meters squared.

items.title: Heat stress enhances Klebsiella pneumoniae -induced cellular injury and impairs milk fat synthesis in bovine mammary epithelial cells.
items.summary: Heat stress (HS) poses a significant threat to dairy production by reducing milk yield and elevating the incidence of mastitis. Concurrently, mastitis caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae ( K. pneumoniae ) occurs more frequently during the summer months, further exacerbating udder health challenges. Our study demonstrates that combined HS and K. pneumoniae exposure significantly exacerbates cellular damage of bovine mammary epithelial cells (BMECs). Mechanistically, HS potentiates K. pneumoniae -induced NF-κB pathway activation and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, leading to upregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and antimicrobial peptides. Simultaneously, HS disrupts tight junction integrity, downregulating ZO-1, Occludin, and Claudins, and compromises the epithelial barrier.

items.title: Microdose jet injection reveals a tissue-dependent retention-expression window for carrier-free nucleic acid delivery.
items.summary: Efficient local nucleic acid delivery requires not only access to target cells but also retention of the administered payload. Yet whether increasing physical delivery input improves or compromises functional delivery remains poorly understood. Here, we show that microdose jet injection operates within a tissue-dependent retention-expression window that can be interpreted in terms of physical jet input. Using the Actranza Lab needle-free system, sub-microlitre to low-microlitre jet outputs were calibrated and characterised by high-speed imaging, defining a kinetic-energy range of approximately 0.38-18.5 mJ. Delivery outcomes were evaluated in mouse spleen, liver, and skin using dye-retention analysis and luciferase expression. In spleen and liver, low-volume jets were associated with local retention and high volume-normalised luciferase expression, whereas increasing jet input progressively increased retention failure and reduced expression efficiency despite larger administered DNA amounts.

items.title: Psychometric properties of a DTD self-report scale among Portuguese adolescents from the community.
items.summary: Background: Developmental Trauma Disorder (DTD) has been proposed as a developmentally informed framework to describe the pervasive dysregulation associated with chronic interpersonal trauma in childhood. DTD has been assessed by a validated structured interview, but no study has validated a self-report measure of DTD symptoms or examined its factorial structure in community adolescent samples. In addition, measurement invariance across sex has not been investigated, despite evidence of sex differences in trauma exposure and trauma-related symptoms. Objective: To evaluate the psychometric properties of a self-report measure of DTD symptoms in a community sample of Portuguese adolescents by testing factorial structure, internal consistency, convergent and discriminant validity, and measurement invariance across sex.

items.title: NADPH oxidase-associated oxidative stress and ferroptosis-related injury in calcium oxalate-exposed renal tubular epithelial cells: pharmacological evidence for PI3K/AKT involvement.
items.summary: Background/objectives Calcium oxalate (CaOx) crystals contribute to renal tubular injury in nephrolithiasis, but the relationship among NADPH oxidase (NOX), oxidative stress, ferroptosis-related injury, and PI3K/AKT signaling remains incompletely defined. We examined CaOx-induced injury in NRK-52E renal tubular epithelial cells and tested the effects of pharmacological NOX and PI3K inhibition on oxidative and ferroptosis-related readouts. Methods NRK-52E cells were exposed to CaOx (0-10 mM) and assessed by CCK-8, DCFH-DA flow cytometry, NOX activity assay, NADPH and Fe 2+ assays, GSH and malondialdehyde (MDA) assays, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), Western blotting, and transcriptome sequencing. Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1, 2 μM), Erastin (10 μM), the NOX inhibitor GKT137831 (10 μM), and the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 μM) were used as pharmacological probes.

items.title: Endpoint-specific mortality associated with malignancy among adults with sepsis or septic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: Background Sepsis is a major global health challenge and increasingly affects patients with complex conditions such as malignancy. Prior studies suggest higher mortality in this population, but interpretation is limited by aggregation of heterogeneous endpoints. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify endpoint-specific prognostic associations between malignancy and mortality in adults with sepsis or septic shock. Methods This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251141216). PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library and Epistemonikos were searched through 16 September 2025, for studies comparing all-cause mortality between sepsis patients with and without malignancy. Mortality endpoints were grouped as ICU, in-hospital, early, intermediate and extended follow-up mortality.
items.author: Chung H, Chou HC, Tsai TY, Chung MC.

items.title: Comparison of an AI-enabled single-lead ECG monitor and point-of-care testing for detecting intradialytic hypokalemia.
items.summary: Background Intradialytic hypokalemia is an underrecognized complication of maintenance hemodialysis (MHD). While point-of-care (POC) testing offers rapid biochemical confirmation, it remains limited by its intermittent nature. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled electrocardiography (ECG) provides a potential noninvasive alternative for trend monitoring; however, its performance in MHD has not been compared with POC testing against a central laboratory standard. Methods This single-center prospective study compared AI-ECG potassium estimation and POC testing during MHD. An algorithm was trained on ECG-potassium pairs from 45 patients (2021-2022) and tested in 29 patients (2023). Concurrent laboratory-POC-ECG pairs enabled direct comparison, using central laboratory assays as the reference standard.
items.author: Chiang WF, Hsiao PJ, Wu KL, Wang RL, Lin KY, Chu CM, Chan JS.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and continuous renal replacement therapy.
items.summary: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is an important intervention in the treatment of acute kidney injury (AKI) in intensive care, and its application scope continues to expand alongside technological advancements and an increasing patient population. However, in current clinical practice, several factors, including individual patient differences, dynamic treatment needs, and the rational allocation of medical resources, pose challenges to CRRT implementation. The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) offers new approaches to address some of these challenges, and its applications in developing decision-support models, refining workflows, and supporting patient communication and education may contribute to more precise and efficient CRRT management.
items.author: Li X, Zhang L.

items.title: Association of non-methane volatile organic compound emission burden with chronic kidney disease: integrated epidemiological, transcriptomic and in vitro analyses.
items.summary: Background Environmental exposure to non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) may contribute to chronic kidney disease (CKD), but the underlying molecular pathways remain unclear. We integrated epidemiological, transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental analyses to identify candidate mechanisms linking NMVOCs to kidney injury. Methods Province-level NMVOC emission burden was linked to residential province for 3,472 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). CKD was defined as an eGFR 2 . Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Putative NMVOC-CKD targets, kidney transcriptomic datasets, 113 machine-learning models, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to prioritize biomarkers. Single-cell transcriptomics, cell-communication analysis, virtual knockout, and hydroquinone-treated cell experiments were used to investigate candidate pathways.

items.title: Kittiwake Committee: Monitoring Black-legged kittiwakes in Homer, Alaska
items.summary: Kittiwake Committee: Monitoring Black-legged kittiwakes in Homer, Alaska Black-legged kittiwake sitting on two chicks in the Homer harbor. (Image credit: Galen June) Download Image November 6, 2026 I’m Galen June, and I’m studying marine biology with a minor in statistics at Old Dominion University. I spent my summer in Homer, Alaska, at the Kachemak Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve (NERR) mentored by Ingrid Harrald. For my research project, I monitored the reproductive success and population of black-legged kittiwake ( Rissa tridactyla ) colonies on Gull Island and in Homer harbor. Here are some highlights from my summer internship as a seabird biologist.

items.title: Quantifying primary productivity in a freshwater estuary in Huron, Ohio
items.summary: Quantifying primary productivity in a freshwater estuary in Huron, Ohio Bryn Fleming collecting American water lotus ( Nelumbo lutea ) in order to measure their rates of photosynthesis and respiration. (Image credit: Jacob Cianci-Gaskill) Download Image November 4, 2026 This summer, I worked with the Old Woman Creek National Estuarine Research Reserve (NERR) as a water quality research intern. My project focused on measuring the rates of oxygen production by different plants and phytoplankton in the estuary. I also calculated overall oxygen flux in the estuary using large time-series datasets collected from water quality monitoring stations. These measurements are important because they tell us about the health of an ecosystem and whether it stores or produces carbon.
